findings.issue: The all-customer loader returns only the first page

findings.impact: Customers after the first page disappear from a consumer that promises all choices. This is selection/completeness loss, not evidence of deletion from persistent storage.

findings.issue: enforce: false bypasses every server-side access check
findings.trigger: The server is started with enforce: false and receives a direct HTTP request from an unknown identity, wrong owner, cross-tenant identity, or a read-only actor using a non-GET method.
findings.impact: The fixture responds 200 with tenant-a resource data regardless of identity/ownership/tenant/write permission. This proves an unsafe selectable branch in the fixture, not a deployed production vulnerability or an actual deletion.
findings.recommended_fix: Keep production enforcement unconditional. If the opt-out is required as a deliberate negative fixture, isolate it in test-only construction and ensure application callers cannot disable the policy. Verify direct request denial across relevant methods.
findings.test_gap: No HTTP denial tests were run or read. Exercise missing/unknown identity, bob (wrong owner), eve (cross tenant), reader GET/non-GET, and alice, with both option values; verify deployment cannot opt out.
findings.evidence: Line 8 initializes status=200; the sole checks at lines 10-11 are entirely nested under if(enforce) at line 9; lines 13-14 return resource data whenever status remains 200.
findings.required_fix: Keep production enforcement unconditional. If the opt-out is required as a deliberate negative fixture, isolate it in test-only construction and ensure application callers cannot disable the policy. Verify direct request denial across relevant methods.
